name: Chennai
tagline: Temple gateways, Carnatic music and a long Bay of Bengal shore.
whenBlurb: November to February is cool and, in Margazhi, alive with the world's greatest Carnatic music season. Avoid the fierce April to June heat and October monsoon.

ourTake.lede: Chennai is a city of temples, music and the sea rather than obvious sights, and it rewards travellers interested in the deep Tamil and Carnatic culture more than casual sightseers. Do the Marina and the San Thome quarter early, and give real time to Mylapore and, ideally, a day trip to the Pallava wonders at Mahabalipuram. The December music season is the reason to time a trip here if culture is your thing.
ourTake.comeIf: You want deep South Indian temple culture, Chettinad cooking and Marina Beach at a gentle domestic pace.
ourTake.skipIf: You are after a resort holiday or nightlife; this is a working city, best for its heritage and its food.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: ITC Grand Chola, a Luxury Collection Hotel
credentials: Marriott, The Luxury Collection (9th hotel in the brand)
LEED, world's largest LEED Platinum hotel; LEED Zero Carbon & LEED Zero Water certified
Houses Avartana, Asia's 50 Best Restaurants (No. 30, 2023)
items.description: A Chola-temple palace in stone, the world's largest LEED Platinum hotel, and the definitive luxury address in the south.

items.name: Taj Coromandel, Chennai
credentials: Taj Hotels, recognised luxury house
Houses Southern Spice, long-recognised benchmark South Indian restaurant
items.description: Chennai's grande dame since 1974, classic Taj service in the heart of the city, and home to the legendary Southern Spice.

items.name: The Leela Palace Chennai
credentials: The Leela Palaces, Hotels & Resorts, recognised luxury house
Recognised leading seafront luxury hotel, Bay of Bengal frontage
items.description: A Chettinad-inspired palace on the Bay of Bengal, Chennai's only true seafront luxury hotel, opulent and calm.

items.name: Park Hyatt Chennai
credentials: Hyatt, Park Hyatt (recognised luxury house)
Houses The Flying Elephant, recognised landmark dining-and-bar destination
items.description: An intimate design-led Hyatt conceived as a 'house of weavers', and home to The Flying Elephant, the city's landmark bar.

items.name: Taj Fisherman's Cove Resort & Spa, Chennai
credentials: Taj Hotels, recognised luxury house
Recognised leading coastal resort, private beach, built within a historic Dutch fort
items.description: A beach resort inside a Dutch fort's ancient walls, 48 garden acres and a private beach on the Bay of Bengal.

items.name: The Raintree, Anna Salai
credentials: Recognised ECOTEL-certified green hotel, pioneering eco-luxury in Chennai
Recognised leading central business hotel
items.description: A polished, genuinely green city hotel, among India's pioneering ECOTEL-certified luxury addresses, central and well-run.

items.name: Crowne Plaza Chennai Adyar Park
credentials: IHG, Crowne Plaza (recognised international house)
Houses Dakshin, recognised regional South Indian restaurant
items.description: A long-standing, well-placed IHG hotel in leafy Alwarpet, home to a much-loved South Indian dining room in Dakshin.

items.name: Hyatt Regency Chennai
credentials: Hyatt, Hyatt Regency (recognised international house)
Houses Q Bar, recognised rooftop bar
items.description: A bright, capable Hyatt Regency on Anna Salai, big rooms, a rooftop bar and dependable international service.

items.name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
items.description: The soul of old Madras, a 7th-century Shiva temple whose 120-foot eastern gopuram rises in a riot of painted stucco gods over the lanes of Mylapore, its inner shrines still thick with camphor and jasmine. Go early for the aarti, then walk the four car-streets around the great temple tank. If you come in Panguni (mid-March to mid-April) the Arupathimoovar festival carries the 63 Nayanmar saints in grand procession through the neighbourhood.

items.name: Mylapore Heritage Walk
items.description: The oldest quarter of Chennai, walked properly: the temple tank at dawn, the flower market where sellers thread mounds of jasmine and marigold, the Sunday morning Kapaleeshwarar precinct, and the narrow agraharam streets that end at the sea and San Thome. A private heritage guide turns an hour's stroll into the whole story of how a Tamil fishing town became a city, best in the cool of early morning.

items.name: San Thome Basilica
credentials: One of only three churches in the world built over an apostle's tomb
items.description: A soaring white neo-Gothic cathedral built over the tomb of the Apostle St Thomas, who is believed to have been martyred in Mylapore in the 1st century, one of only three churches in the world raised over the resting place of an apostle. The gleaming spire is a landmark of the Santhome seafront; the crypt and small museum below make it a quiet, moving stop for every faith.

items.name: Marina Beach & the Promenade
credentials: World's second-longest urban beach (13 km)
items.description: The world's second-longest urban beach, 13 kilometres of sand and a six-kilometre promenade where all of Chennai comes to walk at sunrise and eat sundal and bajji at dusk. Grand as the crowds are, it is the great democratic stage of the city; a private early-morning walk before the heat, past the fishing catamarans being hauled in, is the way to feel it.

items.name: Madras Lighthouse
credentials: Only lighthouse in India with a passenger elevator
items.description: The only lighthouse in India you can ride to the top of, a 46-metre tower on the Marina fitted with an electric elevator, opening onto a ninth-floor gallery with 360-degree views over the Bay of Bengal and the whole sweep of the beach and city skyline. A small, unexpected pleasure, best at golden hour when the coast lights up.

items.name: Government Museum, Bronze Gallery
credentials: Second-oldest museum in India (est. 1851)
World's finest collection of Chola bronzes
items.description: The finest collection of Chola bronzes on earth, some 1,500 lost-wax icons from the 9th to 13th centuries, crowned by the Nataraja of Tiruvalangadu and the Ardhanarisvara of Tiruvenkadu, the cosmic dancer and the god-goddess in a single serene form. Set in a rose-red Indo-Saracenic complex that is the second-oldest museum in India. A guided hour in this one gallery is worth the whole visit.

items.name: Fort St George & the Fort Museum
credentials: First English fortress in India (1644)
items.description: Where the East India Company, and modern Chennai, began in 1644, the first English fortress in India and still a working government seat. The Fort Museum keeps colonial portraits, weapons and one of the earliest Union flags; the ramparts and the story of Madras rising from a strip of sand make this the foundation stone of the city.

items.name: St Mary's Church
credentials: Oldest Anglican church east of Suez (1680)
items.description: The oldest Anglican church east of Suez and the oldest surviving British building in India, tucked inside Fort St George, where Robert Clive was married and Elihu Yale, later founder of Yale University, worshipped. The thick bomb-proof walls, old tombstones and quiet interior are a fascinating counterpoint to the Dravidian temples across town.

items.name: Parthasarathy Temple
credentials: One of the 108 Divya Desams (sacred Vishnu shrines)
items.description: An 8th-century Pallava temple to Krishna as Parthasarathy, Arjuna's charioteer at Kurukshetra, one of the oldest structures in the city and among the 108 Divya Desams sacred to Vaishnavites. The old Triplicane streets, the vast temple tank and the working ritual life make it a living counterpart to the tourist trail.

items.name: Ashtalakshmi Temple
items.description: A modern multi-tiered temple right on Elliot's Beach dedicated to the eight forms of Lakshmi, goddess of wealth, courage, knowledge and progeny, with shrines rising level upon level and the Bay of Bengal breaking just beyond the walls. Serene, uncrowded and beautiful at sunset; an easy, uplifting stop after a walk on Besant Nagar beach.

items.name: Marundeeswarar Temple
items.description: An ancient Shiva temple whose name means 'god of medicine', sages and, by legend, Agastya came here for healing, and devotees still visit for cures. A sprawling Dravidian complex with a great gopuram and tank on the coastal road south, far quieter than Kapaleeshwarar and steeped in the same living ritual.

items.name: Kalakshetra Foundation
credentials: Institute of National Importance (by Act of Parliament, 1994)
items.description: The great academy of the Indian arts, founded in 1936 by Rukmini Devi Arundale to rescue and revive Bharatanatyam and Carnatic music, set on a serene forty-hectare campus of thatched open-air studios under old trees. Come for a morning dance class in progress, the Rukmini Devi museum, or, if timed right, an evening performance in the theatre. An Institute of National Importance.

items.name: DakshinaChitra Heritage Museum
items.description: A living-history village on the coast road, gathering eighteen authentic historic houses transplanted from across the four southern states, a Chettinad mansion, a Kerala Nair house, weavers' and potters' homes, with craftspeople giving live demonstrations of pottery, weaving and puppetry. The single best half-day for understanding South Indian life; go with the family, closed Tuesdays.

items.name: Cholamandal Artists' Village
credentials: Largest artists' commune in India (est. 1966)
items.description: The largest artists' commune in India, founded in 1966 by 38 painters and sculptors from the Madras art school and still owned and run by its members, galleries, studios, a museum and an amphitheatre among casuarina trees near the sea. The birthplace of the Madras Movement in modern Indian art; buy directly from working artists.

items.name: Theosophical Society & the Adyar Banyan
credentials: World headquarters of the Theosophical Society (since 1882)
items.description: 260 acres of green quiet on the Adyar estuary, the world headquarters of the Theosophical Society since 1882, with a great library and gardens, and at its heart the Adyar aala maram, a roughly 450-year-old banyan whose aerial roots once shaded 3,000 people. A rare pocket of stillness in the city; note the restricted visiting hours and closure on Sundays.

items.name: Valluvar Kottam
items.description: A monument shaped like a temple chariot honouring Thiruvalluvar, the great Tamil poet-philosopher of the Thirukkural, all 1,330 couplets of his work inscribed on the corridors around a vast auditorium. A striking, purely Tamil piece of civic architecture and a window into the Dravidian pride in language and letters.

items.name: Ripon Building
items.description: The gleaming all-white neoclassical seat of the Chennai Corporation, one of the grandest colonial buildings in the city, crowned by a Westminster-chime clock tower. Best admired from outside as part of a colonial-architecture drive with Central Station and the High Court, the imperial Madras that sits alongside the temples.

items.name: Chennai Central Station
items.description: The rust-red Indo-Saracenic landmark of the city, a grand 1870s railway terminus with a soaring clock tower, one of the most photographed buildings in South India and the historic gateway to Madras. Even without a train, the façade at dusk is a set-piece of colonial Chennai; pair it with the Ripon Building and the Southern Railway headquarters nearby.

items.name: T Nagar Silk & Jewellery Shopping
items.description: One of the busiest shopping districts in the country and the place Indian families come for weddings, the multi-storey silk emporia of Nalli and Pothys and the vast gold showrooms of GRT and Saravana Stores around Panagal Park. For Kanchipuram silks and temple jewellery there is nowhere denser; a private shopper or advance appointment turns the crush into a calm, seated affair.

items.name: Nalli Silks (Flagship)
items.description: The most storied name in South Indian silk, a family house selling Kanchipuram sarees since 1928, its T Nagar flagship the pilgrimage point for brides and connoisseurs seeking hand-woven pure-zari weaves. Ask for the heritage and bridal floors and the master weaves; staff will lay out saree after saree with practised ceremony.

items.name: Amethyst
items.description: Chennai's original garden-café-and-gallery, a restored colonial mansion set in a lush walled garden, housing the Wild Garden Café, a fashion boutique upstairs, a flower shop and an events folly. The most graceful place in the city for a long lunch or afternoon tea, and a fixture of the design-and-art crowd; leafy, cool and unhurried.

items.name: The December Music Season (Margazhi)
items.description: The largest classical arts festival in the world, through December and early January hundreds of Carnatic music and Bharatanatyam concerts fill the sabhas of the city, from the Music Academy to Narada Gana Sabha, alongside the famous canteen food. For anyone who loves Indian classical arts this is the season to come; book the marquee kacheris and a Mylapore canteen table well ahead.

items.name: The Music Academy
items.description: The most prestigious concert hall for Carnatic music in the world, its Sadas and the awarding of the Sangita Kalanidhi title are the highest honour in the tradition, and its December season stage is where reputations are made. Even off-season, catch a recital here to hear the art at its summit; the acoustics and the crowd are the real thing.

items.name: Filter Coffee & the Mylapore Tiffin Trail
items.description: The daily ritual of the city: degree filter kaapi frothed between two steel tumblers, and crisp dosai, soft idli and pongal at institutions like Murugan Idli Shop and the old Karpagambal Mess by the temple. Vegetarian, excellent and deeply local, a private food walk through Mylapore's messes and coffee houses is the tastiest hour in Chennai.

items.name: Saravana Bhavan
items.description: The Chennai vegetarian institution that went global, impeccable South Indian tiffin, meals on banana leaf and the full sweep of dosai and filter coffee, born here and now on high streets worldwide. Pure-veg, spotless and reliable across every branch; the original city outlets remain a rite of passage for first-time visitors.

items.name: Chettinad Cuisine
items.description: The most celebrated regional cooking of Tamil Nadu, the fiery, aromatic fare of the Chettiar merchant homes, built on freshly roasted spice blends, sun-dried ingredients and dishes like pepper chicken and kara kuzhambu. Seek it at a specialist like The Bangala's Chennai kitchen or a good Chettinad table; a private cook or tasting menu shows its depth beyond the heat.

items.name: Taj Connemara (Heritage Stay)
credentials: Oldest hotel in South India (est. 1854)
items.description: The oldest hotel in South India, opened in 1854 as the Imperial and reborn as an intimate Art-Deco-and-colonial luxury house after a long restoration, with the storied Verandah for tea and a residents' library that once hosted William Dalrymple. Stay here to sleep inside Madras history; even a drink in the bar is a step into the old city.

items.name: Ayurveda & Wellness
items.description: Tamil Nadu takes its Ayurveda and siddha traditions seriously, and Chennai's better spas and coastal retreats along the East Coast Road offer authentic panchakarma, abhyanga and consultations with resident vaidyas. A private, physician-led programme, a morning treatment or a multi-day cleanse, is an easy, restorative counterpoint to temples and shopping.

items.name: Elliot's Beach & Besant Nagar
items.description: The quieter, cleaner beach the city keeps for itself, 'Bessie' to locals, fronted by the Karl Schmidt memorial and lined with cafés and the Ashtalakshmi temple. Calmer and more polished than the Marina, it's the pleasant end of an evening: a seafront stroll, a coffee, and the sea air.

items.name: Semmozhi Poonga Botanical Garden
items.description: A rare green lung in the centre of the city, a landscaped botanical garden of some 500 plant species, glasshouses and shaded walks laid out on old colonial nursery grounds. A cool, calm morning stroll between sightseeing, and an easy stop for a multi-generation group needing a gentle interlude.

items.name: Guindy National Park & Snake Park
credentials: One of the few national parks within a city's limits
items.description: One of the very few national parks inside a major city, a pocket of dry scrub forest with blackbuck, spotted deer and the adjoining Guindy Snake Park's reptile collection, all within the metropolitan limits. A surprising bit of wild for children and grandparents alike, and a reminder of the country the city grew out of.

items.name: Vivekanandar Illam (Ice House)
items.description: A striking circular Marina-front building that once stored ice shipped from America to colonial Madras, later where Swami Vivekananda stayed on his return from Chicago in 1897, now a museum on his life and Indian philosophy. An unusual, atmospheric stop that ties the seafront to a chapter of India's spiritual renaissance.

items.name: Kalakshetra & Craft Shopping, Kalamkari and Weaves
items.description: Beyond silk, Chennai is a doorway to Tamil craft, Kalamkari hand-painted textiles, Thanjavur paintings with gold-leaf and stone inlay, and handloom cottons from state emporia like Poompuhar and Co-optex. A guided shopping morning at the right stores lets a collector buy directly and well, with provenance rather than tourist markup.

items.name: DakshinaChitra Contemporary Art & Crafts Bazaar
items.description: The living-history campus doubles as one of the region's best craft-buying stops, resident artisans sell pottery, weaves, puppets and jewellery, and the site runs workshops and rotating exhibitions. A genuine, un-touristy place to pick up handmade South Indian craft with the maker in front of you.

items.name: Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), Day Trip
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram (1984)
items.description: The great Pallava port-city carved from living granite in the 7th and 8th centuries, the Shore Temple standing against the surf, the monolithic Five Rathas, and Arjuna's Penance, one of the largest open-air rock reliefs in the world. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and an unmissable full day; a private guide and an early start beat the coach crowds.

items.name: The Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Group of Monuments
items.description: The signature image of Tamil Nadu, a granite temple of two Shiva shrines and a Vishnu sanctum built about 700 CE, standing alone at the water's edge and among the oldest structural stone temples in South India. Go at first light or golden hour for the sea, the light and the near-empty enclosure.

items.name: Krishna's Butter Ball, Mahabalipuram
items.description: A colossal natural granite boulder poised at an impossible tilt on a smooth slope, unmoved for centuries despite every attempt to shift it, a favourite for photographs and for children who cannot believe it stays put. A short, delightful stop on the Mahabalipuram monument walk.

items.name: Kanchipuram, Temple Town & Silk (Day Trip)
credentials: Kanchipuram silk saree, Geographical Indication (2005-06)
One of the seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri) of Hinduism
items.description: The 'city of a thousand temples' and one of the seven holiest cities of Hinduism, the vast Ekambareswarar, Kailasanathar and Kamakshi Amman temples, and the source of the world's finest wedding silk, woven here for centuries. Pair the great gopurams with a visit to a weaver's loom; the Kanchipuram silk saree carries its own GI.

items.name: Kailasanathar Temple, Kanchipuram
items.description: The oldest temple in Kanchipuram, an 8th-century Pallava sandstone masterpiece to Shiva, its 58 small shrines and delicate carvings a quieter, older beauty than the town's giant later temples. Serene and rarely crowded; the finest single monument for anyone who cares about early Dravidian architecture.

items.name: Pondicherry, French Quarter & Auroville (Day Trip)
items.description: The old French colony on the Coromandel coast, mustard-yellow villas, bougainvillea, seafront promenade and genuinely good Franco-Tamil cooking in White Town, with the Sri Aurobindo Ashram and the utopian township of Auroville and its golden Matrimandir nearby. Best as an overnight rather than a rushed day; the pace is the point.

items.name: Auroville & the Matrimandir
items.description: The 'city the earth needs', an experimental universal township founded in 1968, at whose centre sits the Matrimandir, a vast golden sphere holding a meditation chamber lit by a single sunbeam through a crystal. Book the inner-chamber visit ahead; the calm and the idealism are unlike anywhere else in the region.

items.name: Tranquebar (Tharangambadi), Day Trip / Overnight
items.description: A forgotten former Danish colony on the sea, the 17th-century Fort Dansborg, a Pandya-era temple and the Danish Governor's house, now the Neemrana 'Bungalow on the Beach' heritage hotel. Remote, atmospheric and unlike any other coastal town in India; best as an overnight woven into a Tanjore-Chettinad heritage loop.

items.name: Vellore, Fort & Golden Temple (Day Trip)
items.description: A near-perfect 16th-century Vijayanagara fort with a moat and the exquisite Jalakandeswarar temple inside, plus the modern Sripuram Golden Temple nearby, a Lakshmi shrine sheathed in real gold. An easy full day of very different sights, best with a private car and driver.

items.name: Chennai's Colonial Architecture Drive
credentials: Madras High Court, one of the largest judicial complexes in the world
items.description: Madras wears its colonial past in stone, the Indo-Saracenic Madras High Court (among the largest court complexes in the world), the University's Senate House, Southern Railway HQ and the Ripon Building. A private morning drive with a heritage guide stitches these red-and-white landmarks into the whole arc from Fort St George to the modern city.

items.name: VGP / ECR Coastal Drive & Beaches
items.description: The drive south along the East Coast Road is a pleasure in itself, casuarina groves, the Muttukadu backwater and boating, artisanal spots and quiet resort beaches strung between the city and Mahabalipuram. A relaxed half-day loop with stops at DakshinaChitra and Cholamandal, ending with lunch by the water.

items.name: Avartana
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, No. 30 (2023), No. 44 (2024)
The World's 50 Best Discovery
TripAdvisor Travellers' Choice, India's No. 1 fine-dining restaurant (2024)
items.description: Modern South Indian reimagined as a chandelier-lit tasting menu, India's most awarded southern kitchen, and a genuine reason to cross the country.

items.name: Kappa Chakka Kandhari
credentials: The World's 50 Best Discovery
Condé Nast Traveller India, Top 50 Restaurants (No. 22)
items.description: A loving revival of Kerala home cooking, tapioca, jackfruit and bird's-eye chilli, from 800 recipes gathered across the state.

items.name: Southern Spice
credentials: Taj Hotels, long-recognised benchmark South Indian restaurant
Recognised at International Hospitality Council honours (2023)
items.description: The definitive fine South Indian dining room, the four southern states on one silver-service menu, in the city that knows them best.

items.name: Dakshin
credentials: Times Food Guide, recognised leading South Indian restaurant
Recognised ITC-heritage South Indian dining concept
items.description: Regal South Indian dining since the 1980s, the four southern states on one grand menu, with appalams poured tableside.

items.name: Peshawri
credentials: ITC Hotels, recognised signature Frontier-cuisine restaurant
The World's 50 Best Discovery, ITC Bukhara/Peshawri lineage
items.description: ITC's celebrated North-West Frontier grill, dal Bukhara simmered overnight, kebabs and breads from the clay tandoor, eaten by hand.

items.name: Saravana Bhavan
credentials: Legendary institution, India's most widely recognised South Indian vegetarian chain (est. 1981)
Global standing, outlets from Chennai to Paris and Dallas
items.description: The South Indian vegetarian institution that went global, the birthplace of the mini-idli, and a benchmark for the everyday classics.

items.name: Annalakshmi
credentials: Legendary institution, long-running charitable vegetarian restaurant (est. 1980s)
Recognised for refined pure-vegetarian dining
items.description: A serene, service-led vegetarian institution run by volunteers, refined Indian cooking with proceeds to charity, run 'with love'.

items.name: Murugan Idli Shop
credentials: Legendary institution, Chennai's best-known idli house (Chennai since 2003)
Widely recognised as the city's benchmark idli
items.description: The idli specialist beloved across the city, feather-soft idlis with a spread of chutneys and a peppery kaara kuzhambu, on a banana leaf.

items.name: Ratna Café
credentials: Legendary institution, one of Chennai's oldest restaurants (est. 1948)
Widely recognised for its iconic sambar-idli
items.description: Since 1948, the modest Triplicane café whose sambar drowns its idlis and whose name generations of Chennai grew up on.

items.name: The Flying Elephant
credentials: Widely recognised as Chennai's landmark bar-and-dining destination
In-hotel at Park Hyatt, recognised luxury house
items.description: A multi-level design landmark that redefined the city's nightlife, golden bars, open grills and Madras-inspired cocktails under one roof.

items.name: Madras Cocktail Company
credentials: Recognised leading speakeasy-style cocktail bar in Chennai
Widely cited among the city's best cocktail rooms
items.description: A password-only speakeasy behind an unassuming door, a compact, spirited room for craft cocktails and a proper night out.

items.name: Q Bar
credentials: Recognised leading rooftop bar in Chennai
In-hotel at Hyatt Regency, recognised international house
items.description: A breezy rooftop atop the Hyatt Regency, panoramic city views, resort-style calm and cocktails with a local twist.

items.name: Radio Room
credentials: Widely recognised leading pub and cocktail bar in Chennai
Recognised for its music-led design and lively scene
items.description: A music-themed pub of album covers and retro props, craft cocktails, small plates and one of the city's liveliest rooms.

plan.heading: 3 days in Chennai, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning walk on Marina beach, then the San Thome basilica and the Portuguese quarter.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Fort St. George and the colonial spine, then the galleries of the Government Museum in Egmore.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Southern Spice in the Taj Coromandel, Chettinad done to the highest standard.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Kapaleeshwarar temple and the tank at Mylapore, the oldest heart of the city.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Drive down the coast to the Mahabalipuram shore temples and the Pancha Rathas.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Seafood by the water at Fisherman's Cove in Covelong, or back in town.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Kanchipuram for the silk-weaving looms, or Kalakshetra for the dance and textile campus.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A leisurely lunch of a banana-leaf meal, then the Amethyst or a heritage bungalow café.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Filter coffee and a final dinner at Avartana in the ITC Grand Chola.

items.name: Mylapore
items.description: The cultural and temple heart of old Madras; best for heritage, music and traditional life.

items.name: Nungambakkam / Boat Club
items.description: The leafy upscale district of restaurants and consulates; suits those wanting comfort and dining.

items.name: ECR (East Coast Road)
items.description: The coastal strip towards Mahabalipuram with beach resorts; for a seaside, resort-style base.

events.name: Margazhi Music Season
events.note: The world's largest classical-music festival, with hundreds of Carnatic concerts across the city; the reason serious culture-lovers come.

events.name: Pongal
events.note: Tamil Nadu's harvest festival, the state's most important, marked with kolam art and feasting.

events.name: Mylapore Festival
events.note: A heritage street festival around the Kapaleeshwarar temple, with kolam contests, crafts and performance.

events.name: Chennai Sangamam
events.note: A large open, free festival of Tamil folk arts staged across public spaces alongside Pongal.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Base yourself around Boat Club Road or the seafront for the best properties and calm; dress modestly for temples such as Kapaleeshwarar and remove shoes; the climate is warm year-round, so plan sightseeing for early morning or evening.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Chennai international airport and be met by a private chauffeur; the airport sits southwest of the centre, about forty-five minutes from the coastal hotels along the Marina and Boat Club Road.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car and driver handles the heat, distances and traffic best; the seafront and Mylapore's temple lanes are pleasant on foot in the cooler hours.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Strong 4G and 5G citywide on all networks; eSIMs and hotel wifi work without issue.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; cards and UPI are widely accepted, with cash useful in older markets and temple areas; ten percent is a standard tip.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: December–February is the window, warm, dry and comfortable by coastal standards. Avoid April–June (hot and very humid) and the October–December northeast monsoon, which can flood the city.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi (~2h45m), Mumbai (~2h) and Bengaluru (~1h) into Chennai (MAA); Air India offers business on the Delhi/Mumbai routes and it is also a strong international gateway. The new T2 terminal is far improved, use the premium lounge, and pre-book a car as the airport-to-city traffic can be heavy.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations beyond routine. Safe and easy for a major metro. No altitude. Heat and humidity are the real load, hydrate. Tap water is not potable; sealed bottled only, and be cautious with roadside food and ice.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: One of the easiest cities in the world for vegetarians, South Indian food is largely veg, and Jain (no onion/garlic) is widely understood. Saravana Bhavan and Murugan Idli Shop are institutions; for refined dining, the vegetarian kitchens at the Taj Coromandel and ITC Grand Chola cook excellent pure-veg and Jain to order.
